title: Fatal Attraction
author: Roger Auman
notes: The Caller's Box 10426, permission: full. The dance travels round the **major** set twice — 156 duple dances in the corpus do — and the promenade is what carries you to N2. A2's first two beats are the milestone's concurrency test: `(2) Women cast back || Men go forward`, two figures over disjoint dancers at the same beats, and they dance. "Men go forward" is a **dance-local figure** (D10). **Still owed, measured.** Closure 68.0000 px at every checked line length (4–12), reach 54.6611 px short, collision 0.000 px. The one thing owed is **`N2` in becket**: `pairs: "N2"` pairs nobody in this dance at any length, so A2's shoulder round and swing and B1's promenade are all inert and only A1's promenade travels — which is exactly the 68 px. Measured on the lattice alone, with no dance in it: in an eight-couple becket set `relatedPairs(model, N2, everybody)` returns **2 pairs of a possible 8**, where duple improper returns 6; N3 returns **0**. The becket relation table is M6's and its own tests pass, so this is a disagreement between M6's table and what a becket dance means by N2 rather than a fault this milestone introduced.

source.transcript:
A1  (8) Ladies chain to neighbor  (8) Neighbor promenade counterclockwise around the major set
A2  (2) Women cast back || Men go forward  (6) N2 neighbor right shoulder round  (8) N2 neighbor swing
B1  (8) N2 neighbor promenade clockwise around the major set  (8) Women allemande right 1 & 1/2
B2  (4) Partner balance  (12) Partner swing

go-forward.describe: On your own, walk forward one place along the line you are standing in, still looking the way you were looking, while the dancer beside you casts back into the place behind them.

walkthrough.short: Walk forward one place along your own line while the dancer beside you casts back.
walkthrough.long: On your own, walk forward one place along the line you are standing in, still looking the way you were looking, while the dancer beside you casts back into the place behind them. Nobody's hand: the two of you are dancing different figures in the same two beats.
